ECE 685 | Power Systems Design L07
Single-Phase AC Circuits III
Power-factor correction with shunt capacitors
Buxin She
Mike Wiegers Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

Lecture outline
1 Calculate capacitor compensation for a target power factor
2 Distinguish absorbed and supplied reactive power
3 Verify the corrected power factor and source current
ECE 685 | Single-Phase AC III 2/18

PART 1
Theory and formulas
Power conventions and the four-step correction method

Load and generator sign conventions
Recall L06: 𝐿 = load, 𝐺 = generator
Load: power absorbed
𝐼𝐿 enters the + terminal.
𝑆𝐿 = 𝑉 𝐿𝐼 ∗
𝐿 = 𝑃 𝐿 + j𝑄𝐿
𝑃𝐿 > 0: absorbs real power.
𝑄𝐿 > 0: absorbs reactive power.
𝑄𝐿 < 0: supplies reactive power.
Generator: power delivered
𝐼𝐺 leaves the + terminal.
𝑆𝐺 = 𝑉 𝐺𝐼 ∗
𝐺 = 𝑃 𝐺 + j𝑄𝐺
𝑃𝐺 > 0: supplies real power.
𝑄𝐺 > 0: supplies reactive power.
𝑄𝐺 < 0: absorbs reactive power.
Positive means absorption at the load and delivery at the generator.
ECE 685 | Single-Phase AC III 4/18

Capacitor power and power balance
The capacitor uses the load convention
𝐼𝐶 enters the + terminal. An ideal capacitor has 𝑃𝐶 = 0.
𝑆𝐶 = 𝑉 𝐼 ∗
𝐶 = j𝑄𝐶 , 𝑄 𝐶 < 0
The source supplies the load and capacitor together
𝑆𝐺 = 𝑆 𝐿 + 𝑆𝐶
𝑃𝐺 = 𝑃 𝐿, 𝑄 𝐺 = 𝑄 𝐿 + 𝑄𝐶
Negative 𝑄𝐶 means reactive power supply. It reduces 𝑄𝐺 while 𝑄𝐿 stays unchanged.

PART 2
Worked example
The L06 load: correction from 0.800 to 0.950 lagging

Worked example: the L06 load
Known load and results from L06
𝑉 = 240∠0 ∘ Vrms, 𝑍 𝐿 = 8 + j6 Ω
𝑃 = 4.608 kW, 𝑄 1 = 3.456 kvar, pf1 = 0.800 lagging
|𝑆𝐺1| = 5.760 kVA, |𝐼 𝐺1| = 24.0 A
Correction target and capacitor conditions
pf2 = 0.950 lagging, 𝑓 = 60 Hz.
Apply Steps 1–4 to this same load using its known initial state.
ECE 685 | Single-Phase AC III 13/18

ECE 685 | Single-Phase AC III 17/18

Correction summary
1 T arget reactive power: 𝑄2 = 𝑃 tan(cos−1 pf2).
2 Required compensation: 𝑄𝐶 = 𝑄 2 − 𝑄1.
3 Capacitance: 𝐶 = |𝑄 𝐶 |/(2𝜋𝑓 𝑉2) at the capacitor terminals.
4 Verification: check net source power, power factor, and current.
At fixed voltage, load power stays unchanged. The capacitor supplies part of the
reactive demand.
